title: SLO-aligned escalation lattices and automated remedial playflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are seeing frequent noisy pages for SLO degradations during short-lived traffic shifts and regional infra flakiness. Pages are generated from single-signal thresholds (p50 latency or 5xx spikes) and often resolve before human intervention, causing on-call fatigue and delayed responses to real incidents.

Goal: Implement an "escalation lattice": a SLO-aligned, multi-signal gating layer that reduces noise by requiring correlated signals and progressive escalation tiers. Pair this with automated remedial playflows (runbook runners) that can perform safe, reversible mitigations (circuit-break triggers, selective load-shedding, and traffic steering) before paging. If automated mitigations fail or cross severity boundaries, escalate to on-call with a compact, context-rich page.

Scope:
- Build gating logic in AlertRouter service to evaluate composite rules (error-rate + p95 latency + region health) with configurable windows and hysteresis.
- Implement probabilistic dedupe & temporal smoothing (token-bucket + short Bloom filter cache) to avoid duplicate pages from correlated downstream metrics.
- Add circuit-breaker policy types: soft-threshold (auto-degrade non-critical routes), hard-threshold (open circuit and redirect), and scoped shedding (drop low-value features first).
- Create automated playflows (playbook runner) that run pre-approved sequences: validate, checkpoint, execute (eg. scale, switch model variant, flip routing), verify, rollback on failure.
- Integrate playflows with runbook docs, PagerDuty (or Opsgenie), and Slack incident channels so humans are only paged for unresolved or high-severity events.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of alerting system; replacing human incident triage entirely; implementing new model quantization strategies.

Success criteria:
- 45% reduction in non-actionable P1 pages for the last 90 days of traffic in canary region within 8 weeks.
- Mean time to acknowledge for pages generated by the lattice should improve (target < 15m for genuine incidents).
- Automated playflows should successfully mitigate at least 30% of incidents that previously required manual intervention in staging/chaos runs.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Window length: use composite windows (short 2m for burst detection + 15m smoothing for sustained issues). Trade-off: longer windows reduce noise but increase detection latency. We bias toward multi-tier escalation to preserve early automation.
- Deduplication: prefer lightweight probabilistic caches to avoid per-alert state blowup. Accept small false negatives but rely on correlation gating to avoid missed incidents.
- Automation safety: playflows must run with a validation stage (canary action + quick verify) and must be limited to low-risk actions by default (scale up/down, route to warm fallback). High-risk actions (DB failover, global evacuations) require manual approval.
- Observability: every automated action emits structured events (runbook-id, step, result) to Console and an audit log for post-incident review.

Artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Escalation+Lattice+Design
- Initial runbook templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Runbook+Templates+2026
- GitHub prototype PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-router/pull/78, https://github.com/redwood-inference/playflow-runner/pull/22
- Dashboard (canary region): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rg1-escalation-lattice

Rollout plan:
1) Implement gating + dedupe in AlertRouter and run in passive (no page) mode for 2 weeks to measure signal fidelity.
2) Deploy playflow runner in staging; author 5 canonical playflows for common incidents (model OOMs, KV cache storms, region network errors, autoscaler misfires, degraded storage).
3) Canary enable automated mitigations in a low-traffic region with strict telemetry. Run chaos experiments to verify safe rollback.
4) Gradually expand to multi-region with per-customer opt-out flags and telemetry gates.

Backstop & rollback: All automated actions are tagged and reversible; a single global kill-switch disables automation. Paging rules keep a fast path to page on high-severity thresholds regardless of automation state.
